what: The world record's own ending, read from the video frame by frame (track END, 2026-10-09). jay_cee 12:29.250, Battletoads NES Any% (No Credits Warp), youtube A7czTlY7OI0 (1280x720, 60.00 fps; the NES runs 60.0988, so 1 video frame = 1.0016467 NES frames).
method: Built-in browser: the YouTube player's frames drawn into a canvas at t = n/60 + 0.008 s for every frame n (745.0-773.0 s, 19.2-22.3 s, 726.7-728.0 s). Game area = x >= 33.5 % of the picture. Signals: mean luminance (cuts to black), 24-cell picture difference (9 identical frames = a hit's freeze; a jump every 4th frame = the camera shake after the dead Queen's bounce), the scroll position of Level 1's horizon (the landing). The same signals were measured on our own capture/emulator to tie each one to a RAM event (end_black.py, logs/fix/land/).

leaderboard.note: 749.250 s x 60 = 44955 video frames exactly, so the board's time is a frame count on this video. Our event definitions (landing = first frame at rest, video 1249; end = the frame the level byte turns 254 = last frame with the status bar still drawn, video 46202) give 44953 frames = 749.217 s: the retime starts/ends one frame wider on each side. CONFIRMED: 749.25 s is the cut to Professor T. Bird, not the cut to the Queen's speech (that is at 740.58 s).

tail.last_hit_height: on the floor (h 44): the first camera shake comes 100 frames after the blow = 9 frozen + 92 of flight

level13.note: we enter Level 13 about 523 frames behind the record (his first black 706.50 s on the landing clock = our-frame 44534; ours 45057), win about 368 in the fight, are 155 behind at the final blow and 152 behind at the T. Bird cut.

clock_offset.note: run time = video time - 20.82 s (landing), or - 20.80 s on the leaderboard's own count. knowledge/wr_splits.json was built with 20.69, so its level ends (not its total) read about 0.12 s (7 frames) late: e.g. Level 12's first black frame is video 727.317 s = 706.50 s after the landing, not 706.63.
